entries.title: 4 wounded in Auburn Gresham shooting
entries.summary: <p>Four people were wounded in a shooting Saturday evening in Auburn Gresham, Chicago police said.</p><p>The victims were on the sidewalk along the 8500 block of South Sangamon Street about 7:17 p.m. when a car pulled alongside them and multiple people in the vehicle fired several shots, police said.</p><p>A 43-year-old man suffered a gunshot wound to his left leg and was taken to University of Chicago Hospital in critical condition, police said.</p><p>A man whose age was unknown was shot in the abdomen and taken to Christ Hospital in critical condition.</p><p>A 34-year-old man was shot in the right leg and a 32-year-old woman suffered a graze wound to her left arm. They both declined treatment at the scene. </p><p>No arrests have been made. </p>

entries.title: Israel Abrams plans to lead No. 4 Montini to a championship three-peat
entries.summary: <p>Montini senior Israel Abrams is one of the best quarterbacks in the country, ranked among the top four by all the national recruiting services. He is also a top-tier talker, quick to turn a phrase that cries out for a headline:</p><p>‘‘We have one mentality, and that is to kill.’’</p><p>‘‘We are going to go 38-0, we will win three state titles and stamp our name in history.’’</p><p>‘‘I don’t have to worry about the guys on this team. The coaches stay locked in, and so do the guys. It is a well-oiled machine.’’</p><p>It is worth noting all the ‘‘wes’’ in those bold statements and all the team goals mentioned. Abrams, a Miami recruit, isn’t thinking about raising his profile a notch to be named the top quarterback in the country. He isn’t boasting about his five-star ranking. He is focused on winning.</p><p>‘‘He’s a coach’s dream,’’ Montini coach Mike Bukovsky said. ‘‘He loves to play the game. We’ve never had one instance or issue with him not wanting to practice or anything like that. He always loves to compete, to challenge himself and to be challenged.’’</p><p>Abrams is 6-4 and nearing 200 pounds. Bukovsky is thrilled with the weight and muscle Abrams added during the offseason after he threw for 4,072 yards and led the Broncos to an undefeated season and the Class 4A state title in 2025. Abrams was 233-for-340 with 40 touchdown passes and six interceptions. He also scored 10 rushing TDs.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-e30000" name="image-e30000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8e74006/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5814x3263+0+0/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe5%2F98%2Fe8904f374409b469d2f18d7982af%2Fob-cst-081226-009.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/11dfcf3/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5814x3263+0+0/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe5%2F98%2Fe8904f374409b469d2f18d7982af%2Fob-cst-081226-009.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e8d991e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5814x3263+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe5%2F98%2Fe8904f374409b469d2f18d7982af%2Fob-cst-081226-009.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Montini’s Gavin Ericson-Staton (gold shirt) works a drill during preseason practice. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e8d991e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5814x3263+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe5%2F98%2Fe8904f374409b469d2f18d7982af%2Fob-cst-081226-009.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/54da766/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5814x3263+0+0/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe5%2F98%2Fe8904f374409b469d2f18d7982af%2Fob-cst-081226-009.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e8d991e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5814x3263+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe5%2F98%2Fe8904f374409b469d2f18d7982af%2Fob-cst-081226-009.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Montini’s Gavin Ericson-Staton (gold shirt) works a drill during preseason practice.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Kirsten Stickney/For the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>‘‘[Abrams] is detailed in how he attacks things,’’ Bukovsky said. ‘‘He is always interested in that aspect of the game, watching film and studying. That is the backbone of his character. And his arm might be even stronger than last year.’’</p><p>Seniors Luca Florio, Damacio Ortegon and Johnny Neustadt return, and Donovan Evans transferred in from St. Rita. Bukovsky says it is the best corps of wide receivers in school history.</p><p></p><p>‘‘They are going to be looking to eat, and I am going to get the ball to them,’’ Abrams said.</p><p></p><p>Montini, which is ranked No. 4 in the preseason Super 25, has won 24 consecutive games. Abrams took over the starting job during his sophomore year and led the Broncos to the Class 3A title. Seven starters return on offense and five on defense from the Class 4A championship team last season.</p><p></p><p>‘‘The only negative with us this year is we aren’t a super-deep team,’’ Bukovsky said. ‘‘But that’s natural for a school our size. Five hundred twenty-five kids. And that is coed. We are always going to be chasing depth a little bit.’’</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-hangRight><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-320000" name="module-320000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><b>Montini schedule</b><br><ul id="rte-1604de22-9905-11f1-ab6e-51b817acc95d"><li><b>Aug. 21</b> vs. Hoopeston</li><li><b>Aug. 28</b> at Sandburg</li><li><b>Sep. 4</b> at Marist</li><li><b>Sep. 11</b> at Nazareth</li><li><b>Sep. 18</b> vs. Carmel</li><li><b>Sep. 25</b> vs. St. Rita</li><li><b>Oct. 2</b> at De La Salle</li><li><b>Oct. 9</b> vs. Marmion</li><li><b>Oct. 16</b> vs. St. Francis</li></ul></div> </div><p>Starting offensive linemen Michael Lombardo (6-1, 280 pounds), Hunter Mancione (6-5, 265) and Gavin Ericson-Staton (6-6, 285) return. How many state championships did all of the state’s phenomenal superstar QBs win over the last decade or so? [Abrams] is probably at the top of the list.’’</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-3c0000" name="html-embed-module-3c0000"></a><blockquote class="tiktok-embed" cite="https://www.tiktok.com/@michaelsobriensports/video/7674409927347129631" data-video-id="7674409927347129631" style="max-width: 605px;min-width: 325px;" > <section> <a target="_blank" title="@michaelsobriensports" href="https://www.tiktok.com/@michaelsobriensports?refer=embed">@michaelsobriensports</a> Montini is ranked No. 4 in the preseason Super 25. #<a title="ihsa" target="_blank" href="https://www.tiktok.com/tag/ihsa?refer=embed">#ihsa</a> <a title="football" target="_blank" href="https://www.tiktok.com/tag/football?refer=embed">#football</a> <a title="montini" target="_blank" href="https://www.tiktok.com/tag/montini?refer=embed">#montini</a> <a target="_blank" title="♬ original sound - michaelsobriensports" href="https://www.tiktok.com/music/original-sound-7674409885756377886?refer=embed">♬ original sound - michaelsobriensports</a> </section> </blockquote> <script async src="https://www.tiktok.com/embed.js"></script> </div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: Matt Shaw expected to head out on rehab assignment this week
entries.summary: <p>Matt Shaw, slotted as the Cubs super-utility man this season, may be nearing a return from a sprained left hand that’s sidelined him since June 28.</p><p> </p><p>“I think we’re basically at a point where we’re considering a rehab assignment very soon, manager Craig Counsell said before Saturday’s 8-4 loss to St. Louis.</p><p> </p><p>At Triple-A Iowa maybe this week?</p><p> </p><p>“That’s what we’re on pace for,” Counsell said.</p><p> </p><p>Counsell said Shaw hit off a Trajekt high-velocity pitching machine and swung and missed, which is part of the rehab process. The manager said Shaw felt great on Friday and was scheduled to repeat the exercise on Saturday.</p><p> </p><p>Shaw was projected in the super-utility role after the Cubs signed third baseman Alex Bregman to his $175 million, five year free agent contract. Shaw has played six positions this season, with 26 game appearances in right field, followed by second base (seven games), third base (five games), left field (two games), first base (two games) and center field (one game).</p><p> </p><p>He stepped in as the Cubs primary right fielder for 12 games after Seiya Suzuki hurt his right knee on June 13.</p><p> </p><p>In 56 games, the 24-year-old Shaw is batting .246 with four homers and 20 RBIs. He's on his second stint on the IL, after sitting out May 20 to June 9 with mid-back tightness. </p><p> </p><p><b>Wrangling Over “The W”</b></p><p> </p><p>Major League Baseball doesn’t want the WNBA to have unchecked control of “The W.”</p><p> </p><p>The WNBA, its teams and players have been using “The W” to refer to the league in an overall branding strategy. In March 2025, the WNBA <a class="Link" href="https://tmsearch.uspto.gov/search/search-results/99105898" target="_blank" >filed a trademark application</a> for use of “The W” on apparel such as jersey, shirts and caps.</p><p> </p><p>With the Cubs and Washington Nationals in mind, Major League Baseball filed a joint opposition to the trademark application on Aug. 10 to slow the process down establish clear distinctions with versions of the “W” used by those two clubs.</p><p> </p><p>The concern: The WNBA’s use of the“The W” could create confusion and issues with the Cubs white-and-blue “W” win flags that fly on Wrigley Field’s center field scoreboard after victories. The Cubs use that “W” mark on a variety of merchandise. Even bigger, MLB wants to protect the Nationals’ primary script “W” logo that appears on the club’s caps and uniforms, as well as merchandise. </p><p> </p><p>MLB manages trademarks and intellectual property not only for itself and the National and American Leagues, but member teams through “consultation and conversation” with them.</p><p> </p><p>Published reports that originated with Front Office Sports, said MLB has been in regular contact with the WNBA and and NBA, which own 42 % of the women’s league. The goal is to establish boundaries for use of “The W” trademark.</p><p> </p><p>A source at MLB confirmed the businesslike and ongoing dialog, and that it has been amicable. MLB filed the joint opposition for more time to “hash out the details."</p><p> </p><p> </p><p><b>Palencia Progressing</b></p><p>Closer Daniel Palencia, out with right elbow inflammation since June 16, is making progress in his rehab process.</p><p></p><p>The right-hander is scheduled to pitch in Sunday for Triple-A Iowa after being elevated from Double-A Knoxville, where he tossed a strong scoreless inning on Thursday.</p><p></p><p>“He had a nice outing in Knoxville in his last one, and hopefully build on that again tomorrow in Iowa,” Counsell said.</p><p> </p><p><b>More Báez Banter</b></p><p>More on St. Louis outfielder Joshua Báez, who made history with homers in his first three major-league at-bats in Saturday’s 8-4 Cardinals win.</p><p>• Baez became the fourth player this season to go deep in his first major-league at bat, joining Cleveland’s Chase DeLauter, Philadelphia’s Felix Reyes and Detroit’s Eduardo Valencia.</p><p>• He became the sixth Cardinal to homer on the first pitch he ever faced. The most recent previously was pitcher Adam Wainwright, in 2006.<br></p>
